c01.display: Welcome back to NLP, Simply Explained. This is unit 2, lesson 2: part-of-speech tagging.
c01.spoken: Welcome back to N L P, Simply Explained. This is unit 2, lesson 2: part-of-speech tagging.

c02.display: Last time we looked inside words. Today we look at the job each word does in a sentence.
c02.spoken: Last time we looked inside words. Today we look at the job each word does in a sentence.

c03.display: Here is the idea for today. The same word can play different roles in different sentences. Part-of-speech tagging works out which role it's playing.
c03.spoken: Here is the idea for today. The same word can play different roles in different sentences. Part-of-speech tagging works out which role it's playing.

c04.display: A part of speech is the grammatical role a word plays in a sentence: noun, verb, adjective, and so on.
c04.spoken: A part of speech is the grammatical role a word plays in a sentence: noun, verb, adjective, and so on.

c05.display: In "book a flight", the word "book" is a verb. It's something you do.
c05.spoken: In "book a flight", the word "book" is a verb. It's something you do.

c06.display: Think of words as actors. The same actor can play the hero in one film and the villain in the next. You can only tell which by watching the scene.
c06.spoken: Think of words as actors. The same actor can play the hero in one film and the villain in the next. You can only tell which by watching the scene.

c07.display: A tagger gives every word a short label called a tag. Here are six you'll see everywhere.
c07.spoken: A tagger gives every word a short label called a tag. Here are six you'll see everywhere.

c08.display: NOUN is a thing or an idea, like "cat" or "flight".
c08.spoken: NOUN is a thing or an idea, like "cat" or "flight".

c09.display: VERB is an action or a state, like "run", or "book" when you book something.
c09.spoken: VERB is an action or a state, like "run", or "book" when you book something.

c10.display: ADJ, short for adjective, describes a noun, like "happy" or "red".
c10.spoken: ADJ, short for adjective, describes a noun, like "happy" or "red".

c11.display: DET, short for determiner, points to a noun, like "the" or "a".
c11.spoken: DET, short for determiner, points to a noun, like "the" or "a".

c13.display: And PRON is a pronoun, a word that stands in for a noun, like "she" or "it".
c13.spoken: And PRON is a pronoun, a word that stands in for a noun, like "she" or "it".

c14.display: Let's tag a whole sentence: "I want to book a flight".
c14.spoken: Let's tag a whole sentence: "I want to book a flight".

c17.display: "to" gets its own small tag, PART, because here it's part of the verb that follows.
c17.spoken: "to" gets its own small tag, PART, because here it's part of the verb that follows.

c18.display: "book" is a verb: booking is the action.
c18.spoken: "book" is a verb: booking is the action.

c21.display: Notice that "book" was a verb there. But it isn't always.
c21.spoken: Notice that "book" was a verb there. But it isn't always.

c22.display: In "book a flight", it's a verb: an action you do.
c22.spoken: In "book a flight", it's a verb: an action you do.

c23.display: In "read a book", it's a noun: a thing you hold in your hands.
c23.spoken: In "read a book", it's a noun: a thing you hold in your hands.

c24.display: The spelling is identical, so the word alone can't tell you which it is.
c24.spoken: The spelling is identical, so the word alone can't tell you which it is.

c25.display: What decides it is the company it keeps. The neighbouring words decide.
c25.spoken: What decides it is the company it keeps. The neighbouring words decide.

c26.display: So how does a tagger make the decision? It works in three steps.
c26.spoken: So how does a tagger make the decision? It works in three steps.

c27.display: Look up: first it checks which tags each word is able to take. "book" could be a noun or a verb.
c27.spoken: Look up: first it checks which tags each word is able to take. "book" could be a noun or a verb.

c28.display: Check neighbours: then it looks at what usually comes before and after each tag.
c28.spoken: Check neighbours: then it looks at what usually comes before and after each tag.

c29.display: Pick the best: finally it chooses the tags that make the most sense for the whole sentence together, not just one word at a time.
c29.spoken: Pick the best: finally it chooses the tags that make the most sense for the whole sentence together, not just one word at a time.

c30.display: What kinds of clues does a tagger learn? Here are four simple ones.
c30.spoken: What kinds of clues does a tagger learn? Here are four simple ones.

c31.display: After "the" or "a", the next word is usually a noun.
c31.spoken: After "the" or "a", the next word is usually a noun.

c32.display: After "to", there's often a verb, as in "to book".
c32.spoken: After "to", there's often a verb, as in "to book".

c33.display: A word ending in "l y" is often an adverb, like "quickly".
c33.spoken: A word ending in "l y" is often an adverb, like "quickly".

c34.display: And a word ending in "e d" or "i n g" is often a verb, like "walked" or "walking".
c34.spoken: And a word ending in "e d" or "i n g" is often a verb, like "walked" or "walking".

c35.display: How good are taggers? On English news text, they are very good.
c35.spoken: How good are taggers? On English news text, they are very good.

c36.display: Just picking each word's most common tag already gets about ninety-two percent of words right.
c36.spoken: Just picking each word's most common tag already gets about ninety-two percent of words right.

c37.display: Modern taggers, which use the whole sentence, reach about ninety-seven percent. That still means roughly one word in thirty gets the wrong tag, and the hard cases are exactly the ambiguous ones.
c37.spoken: Modern taggers, which use the whole sentence, reach about ninety-seven percent. That still means roughly one word in thirty gets the wrong tag, and the hard cases are exactly the ambiguous ones.

c38.display: Time for a quick quiz. In the sentence "Time flies like an arrow", what part of speech is "flies"?
c38.spoken: Time for a quick quiz. In the sentence "Time flies like an arrow", what part of speech is "flies"?

c39.display: Pause the video and choose: noun, verb, or adjective?
c39.spoken: Pause the video and choose: noun, verb, or adjective?

c40.display: It's a verb: flying is what time does. But in "Fruit flies like a banana", "flies" is a noun. Same word, different neighbours.
c40.spoken: It's a verb: flying is what time does. But in "Fruit flies like a banana", "flies" is a noun. Same word, different neighbours.

c41.display: Let's recap. A part of speech is the role a word plays in a sentence.
c41.spoken: Let's recap. A part of speech is the role a word plays in a sentence.

c42.display: A tagger labels every word with a tag, like NOUN, VERB or DET.
c42.spoken: A tagger labels every word with a tag, like NOUN, VERB or DET.

c43.display: Many words, like "book", can take more than one tag.
c43.spoken: Many words, like "book", can take more than one tag.

c44.display: And the neighbouring words decide which tag fits.
c44.spoken: And the neighbouring words decide which tag fits.

c45.spoken: Next lesson: Word Vectors. How can a computer know that 'rain' is close to 'storm'?
